about: Physics blocks whose maths is a formula (ND3b): each keeps its id, ports and results, and its maths is the Equation below, with a name that says what happens.

params.description: thermal conductivity of the liquid alloy (Pozzo et al. 2012 give about 150; Konopkova et al. 2016 about 30, measured on solid iron; until MP21's iron rows)
thermal expansivity of the liquid alloy
specific heat of the liquid alloy

references: Labrosse, S. 2015, Physics of the Earth and Planetary Interiors 247, 36: thermal evolution of the core with a high thermal conductivity (the adiabatic heat flow q = k α g T / c_p). doi:10.1016/j.pepi.2015.02.002

Driscoll, P. and Bercovici, D. 2014, Physics of the Earth and Planetary Interiors 236, 36: on the thermal and magnetic histories of Earth and Venus (dynamo power from the CMB flux above the adiabat plus inner core buoyancy). doi:10.1016/j.pepi.2014.08.004
atoms.shown: q_conv = q − k α g T / c_p

equation.name: Heat the core sheds by churning
equation.formula: Fc = q - k * alpha * g * T / max(cp, tiny)

tiny.name: floor that keeps the division finite

alpha.name: how much it expands when hot

cp.name: specific heat of the liquid metal

Fc.name: heat carried by churning, beyond what conducts

source.text: Labrosse, S. 2015, Phys. Earth Planet. Inter. 247, 36

explain.curious: A hot core can lose heat and still make no field: if conduction alone can carry the heat away, the iron does not need to churn.
explain.science: Liquid iron conducts heat well, so part of what leaves the core's top is carried by conduction along the adiabat, q_ad = k α g T / c_p. Only the rest is carried by convection, and only convection stirs a dynamo. When the flux falls below q_ad the top of the core is stably layered.

params.description: fractional density contrast of what is let out (light elements at the inner core boundary, about 5%)
thermal expansivity of the liquid alloy
specific heat of the liquid alloy

references: Buffett, B. A., Huppert, H. E., Lister, J. R. and Woods, A. W. 1996, Journal of Geophysical Research 101, 7989: on the thermal evolution of the Earth's core (light elements released at the inner core boundary as a buoyancy source). doi:10.1029/95JB03539

Driscoll, P. and Bercovici, D. 2014, Physics of the Earth and Planetary Interiors 236, 36: on the thermal and magnetic histories of Earth and Venus (dynamo power from the CMB flux above the adiabat plus inner core buoyancy). doi:10.1016/j.pepi.2014.08.004
O'Rourke, J. G. and Stevenson, D. J. 2016, Nature 529, 387: powering Earth's dynamo with magnesium precipitation from the core. doi:10.1038/nature16495

equation.name: Dynamo power from light elements rising
equation.formula:
Fl = if mdot <= 0 then 0 else cp / max(alpha, tiny) * drho * mdot
Fd = Fc + Fl

mdot.name: light elements let out per square metre per second

tiny.name: floor that keeps the division finite

drho.name: density contrast of what is let out

alpha.name: how much it expands when hot

cp.name: specific heat of the liquid metal

Fd.name: power that drives the dynamo, as a heat flux

source.text: Buffett, B. A., Huppert, H. E., Lister, J. R. and Woods, A. W. 1996, J. Geophys. Res. 101, 7989
source.where: buoyancy at the inner core boundary

explain.curious: Earth's field may be older than its solid inner core. Once the inner core began to freeze, the light elements it pushed out rose like bubbles and gave the dynamo a second engine.
explain.science: A freezing inner core rejects light elements into the liquid above, and magnesium oxide can come out of solution at the core's top; either way buoyant fluid stirs the core. Its power is written as the heat flux that would give the same buoyancy, (c_p/α) Δρ/ρ ṁ/A, and added to the convected flux. A negative convected flux is a stable layer that the buoyancy must first overcome.

params.description: Ro = c Ra_Q*^b: the coefficient (Christensen and Aubert 2006)
Ro = c Ra_Q*^b: the power (Christensen and Aubert 2006)

references: Christensen, U. R. and Aubert, J. 2006, Geophysical Journal International 166, 97: scaling properties of convection-driven dynamos in rotating spherical shells; Ro = c Ra_Q*^b with Ra_Q* = (α g q / ρ c_p) / (Ω³ D²), and dynamos need Rm above about 40 to 50. doi:10.1111/j.1365-246X.2006.03009.x
atoms.shown: u = c Ω D (α g q / (ρ c_p Ω³ D²))^b

equation.name: How fast a conducting layer stirs
equation.formula:
f = g * a * q / (rho * cp)
w = 2 * pi / P
ra = max(f, 0) / ((w * w * w) * (D * D))
u = c * w * D * ra ^ b
ro = u / (w * D)

q.name: power stirring the layer, as a flux through its top

u.name: typical speed of the stirring flow

ro.name: flow speed over spin speed across the layer

source.text: Christensen, U. R. and Aubert, J. 2006, GJI 166, 97
source.where: the Rossby number against the flux-based Rayleigh number, over their dynamo models

explain.curious: Heat and sinking material churn a planet's liquid core, and its spin twists the churning into columns. Earth's core flows at about a millimetre a second, slow as a snail but fast enough, over a core three thousand kilometres deep, to make a field.
explain.science: Christensen and Aubert's scaling for convection in rotating shells: the flow's Rossby number u/(ΩD) is c Ra_Q*^b, where Ra_Q* is the buoyancy flux α g q /(ρ c_p) over Ω³ D². The geometric factor of their definition (outer over inner radius) is left out, so a full sphere has a finite answer. No power, no flow.

references: Christensen, U. R. and Aubert, J. 2006, Geophysical Journal International 166, 97: scaling properties of convection-driven dynamos in rotating spherical shells; Ro = c Ra_Q*^b with Ra_Q* = (α g q / ρ c_p) / (Ω³ D²), and dynamos need Rm above about 40 to 50. doi:10.1111/j.1365-246X.2006.03009.x
Moffatt, H. K. 1978, Magnetic Field Generation in Electrically Conducting Fluids, Cambridge University Press: free decay of a field in a conducting sphere, τ = D² / (π² η)
atoms.shown: Rm = u D μ0 σ;  τ = D² μ0 σ / π²

equation.name: Whether stirring outruns the leak
equation.formula:
eta = 1 / (mu * s)
rm = u * D / eta
tau = (D * D) / (pi * pi * eta)

tau.name: time an unstirred field takes to leak away

source.text: Christensen, U. R. and Aubert, J. 2006, GJI 166, 97
source.where: the magnetic Reynolds number Rm = uD/η; free decay τ = D²/(π²η) after Moffatt 1978

explain.curious: A field in a conductor slowly leaks away unless something keeps stretching it. Liquid iron leaks slowly enough that a millimetre-a-second flow wins; salty water leaks so fast that no ocean makes its own field.
explain.science: The magnetic diffusivity is η = 1/(μ0 σ), from the matter's own conductivity. Rm = uD/η compares stretching with leaking; τ = D²/(π² η) is how long a field lasts with no stirring at all (Keep): thousands of years for a dead planetary core, longer than the age of the universe for a star.

params.description: Rm below which no dynamo runs (Christensen and Aubert 2006: about 40 to 50)
Rm above which it runs fully

references: Christensen, U. R. and Aubert, J. 2006, Geophysical Journal International 166, 97: scaling properties of convection-driven dynamos in rotating spherical shells; Ro = c Ra_Q*^b with Ra_Q* = (α g q / ρ c_p) / (Ω³ D²), and dynamos need Rm above about 40 to 50. doi:10.1111/j.1365-246X.2006.03009.x

equation.name: Whether a dynamo runs
equation.formula: s = if hi <= lo then (if rm >= lo then 1 else 0) else clamp((rm - lo) / (hi - lo), 0, 1)

s.name: how far the dynamo runs, 0 to 1

source.text: Christensen, U. R. and Aubert, J. 2006, GJI 166, 97
source.where: no self-sustained dynamos below Rm of about 40

explain.curious: A dynamo either runs or it does not: below a certain stirring the field dies whatever you do, above it the field grows until it pushes back on the flow.
explain.science: Self-sustained dynamos in rotating shells need Rm above about 40 to 50. That is a real threshold (a bifurcation), so a narrow edge is honest; its width here is the spread across simulations.

params.description: Rossby number below which the field is saturated (Reiners et al. 2022: about 0.13)
how fast the field falls above it (Reiners et al. 2022: Ro^-1.26)

references: Reiners, A. et al. 2022, A&A 662, A41: magnetism, rotation and nonthermal emission in cool stars; the average field saturates below Rossby number about 0.13 and falls as Ro^-1.26 above it. doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202243251
atoms.shown: Ro = P u / D;  factor = 1 below saturation, (sat / Ro)^k above

equation.name: Whether spin is fast enough to organise the field
equation.formula:
ro = P * u / D
f = if ro <= sat then 1 else (sat / ro) ^ k

f.name: factor on the field from spin

source.text: Reiners, A. et al. 2022, A&A 662, A41
source.where: average fields of 292 M dwarfs against Rossby number

explain.curious: Spin organises a dynamo. Every planet spins fast for its slow churning, even Venus, so spin never limits a planet's field; slowly spinning stars churn fast enough that their fields weaken as they spin down.
explain.science: The Rossby number is the spin period over the stirring time D/u. Below about 0.13 the field is saturated; above, it falls as Ro^-1.26 (Reiners et al. 2022). One curve, so planets and stars are the same calculation.
